results.rationale: The slash makes first and second positional-only. Argument 0 binds first, argument 1 binds second; only second is returned.
Keyword spelling, not source order, maps y to right and x to left. Only right is returned.
The explicit x binds data and the omitted ignored parameter uses its None default. The unused entry parameter y has no data path.
The head is constant; x and y bind distinct elements of rest. rest[1] returns y and excludes x.
Both named arguments are collected in values, retaining their keys. Selecting right returns y and excludes x.
Expanding a two-element tuple binds x to first and y to second. The exact tuple shape is available without executing code.
Unknown-length positional expansion fills ignored only; the explicit result keyword independently binds y. No positional element is returned.
A literal dictionary with unique known string keys expands exactly: x binds left and y binds right.
toolkit is an unmodified module import alias; its identity attribute resolves to helpers.identity and preserves x.
imported_identity is an unmodified from-import alias for helpers.identity.
The explicit imports cases -> facade -> bridge -> helpers identify one underlying function definition; no source file is missing.
chosen receives the imported function object without rebinding or branching, preserving its signature and return dependency.

The local assignment shadows the module import. callback has no known definition; importing helpers.identity must not create a false target. Its call result is returned, but input-to-result dependence is unknown.
The first identity result is discarded. Only the second call occurrence contributes its return, preserving y and excluding x.
Under nominal Worker instance dispatch, self supplies the implicit receiver and x supplies data. echo returns data without returning its receiver.
receiver aliases self without mutation. Nominal Worker dispatch retains the same implicit receiver and explicit data mapping.
The unshadowed builtin staticmethod descriptor does not prepend self or cls. The only explicit argument binds data.
The unshadowed builtin classmethod descriptor supplies Descriptors as cls; x binds data, not cls.
Under nominal Inherited instance dispatch, its sole base supplies echo. No local echo shadows Base.echo.
Override.echo takes precedence over Base.echo under nominal Override instance dispatch. The second explicit value y is returned; x is discarded.
Base.echo is retrieved explicitly from the defining class and called unbound. Explicit argument 0 is self and argument 1 is data.
Zero-argument super in the nominal ParentDispatch method searches its sole Base. The resulting bound echo receives self implicitly and x as data.
replace executes during definition and replaces the original identity body with replace.replacement, which ignores data and returns None. The stale original body must not invent x-to-return flow.
The external module is intentionally absent. Its definition and formal names are unknown, while the result of this call directly reaches the entry return. No input-to-return oracle is asserted.
The nested selection evaluates exactly to y.
Index -2 of three elements selects only y.
The reversed stride yields [z, x], excluding y.
Slicing produces [y, z]; its new index zero is y.
The invalid literal index raises; the handler returns fallback, never x.
The returned dictionary explicitly contains the supplied key and value.
The final chosen entry is y even if the earlier dynamic key equals chosen; lookup never returns key or x.
The missing literal key makes get return fallback; the unrelated stored x is not selected.
The later key entry overwrites the unpacked x with y.
The alias refers to the same dictionary; its write replaces x with y.
The selected alias is the inner list itself; clearing it removes x from the returned outer list.
The outer list still holds the original inner list containing x after the local is rebound to [y].
The first list element is a self-reference, while the selected second element is exactly x.
list.append always returns None, despite storing x as a side effect.
When flag is true the result contains x; flag is only a branch condition.
When flag is false the result retains x; neither branch stores flag.
Both normal branch exits return an empty list, so neither parameter contributes content.
push_value stores x into the caller's list; its implicit None return is discarded.
clear_values removes x from the returned list; x nevertheless reaches the callee values parameter before the mutation.
The one-iteration comprehension puts both key and value into the returned mapping.
Selected items come from values; predicate only decides membership and is never stored.
Iteration over an empty tuple yields an empty list without storing x.
The enclosing item remains outside because comprehension variables have their own scope; its result is discarded.
For successful string arguments, join derives its returned string from both iterable elements.
pop(0) returns only the first element x; y remains in the local list and is discarded.
Depth one retains call-site binding and return edge while marking unexpanded implementation.
With helper implementation expanded the parameter reaches the caller return.
Restricted file set has the call expression but no callee definition. Return endpoint still exists; no formal binding oracle is asserted.
One-function budget stops expansion with an explicit budget boundary.
One-call budget cannot cover both syntactic calls; it must report truncation.
A later unconditional assignment kills the earlier value; the result contains y only.
flag controls execution but is never used as a produced value; both branches return x.
Either data operand may be returned; selecting an operand is control dependence, so flag is excluded.
Python and returns an operand: a falsy flag itself or x, so both have actual value flow.
A skipped loop returns x; one taken iteration assigns y then breaks. flag affects control only.
Unconditional continue makes the following assignment unreachable; iteration over y does not modify the returned x.
A taken break returns x and suppresses loop else; otherwise loop else selects y. flag is not data in the result.
The explicitly raised ValueError is caught by the second handler, never the TypeError handler.
The finally return replaces the pending identity(x) result; x still flows into the call but its result is discarded.
Returning a scalar evaluates value before finally; rebinding the local variable does not change the pending result.
An unconditional raise prevents the later return from executing; no input has a normal return path.
The nested closure reads the shared binding at invocation, after value was replaced by y.
The default evaluates x at nested function definition; later rebinding x to y does not update the saved default.
Calling replace assigns y to the enclosing value binding through nonlocal, replacing x before return.
A direct local lambda call returns its argument unchanged.
x reaches discard.value, but discard returns a constant. Callee result still reaches the caller return.
identity receives x but its result is discarded; only y reaches the caller return.
The inner identity result is the outer identity argument, and both calls preserve x.
For nonnegative integer remaining, recursion terminates and swaps a/b on each edge; both are possible results. remaining only controls termination.
No base case produces a normal result; recursively passing x must not invent an x-to-return path.
Selecting the second item of the callee tuple forwards y and excludes the first item x.
Awaiting async_identity executes its body and produces x as the result of the enclosing coroutine.
Calling async_append only creates an unawaited coroutine, so its list mutation never executes and result stays empty.
Advancing generate_one with next obtains its first yielded x; generation and consumption form a real value path.
Creating a generator does not execute the body. Without iteration its append does not run, so result is empty.
CPython str host contract: both result substrings derive from host; None on a delimiter-free path does not erase the other may-flow paths.
CPython attr=value partition returns substrings derived from attr; documented input is str.
Host survives rpartition and/or integer conversion; defport is returned on the missing or empty port branch. Both parameters have normal-execution value paths.
The parameter only selects between constant str/bytes separators. There is control dependence but no explicit parameter value propagation.
